features.name: SD Host Controller 3.0 Compliance
features.description:
## SD Host Controller 3.0 Compliance (F_SD_HOST_3_0)

This feature indicates that the SDMMC Controller implements the SD Host Controller Standard Specification Version 3.0, ensuring compatibility with the standardized register interface, command protocols, and operational modes defined by the SD Association. The controller provides the complete SD Host Controller 3.0 register set including command/response handling, data transfer modes (PIO/DMA/SDMA), clock control, power management, and interrupt mechanisms as specified in the standard. As a P0 core compliance feature, this forms the foundational architecture upon which all other SDMMC functionality is built, guaranteeing interoperability with standard SD/SDIO/eMMC device drivers and software stacks.

features.name: MMC 4.51 Support
features.description:
## MMC 4.51 Support (F_MMC_4_51)

**Feature Description:**

This feature provides compliance with the JEDEC MMC (MultiMediaCard) specification version 4.51, enabling the SDMMC Controller to interface with eMMC (embedded MMC) devices commonly used for non-volatile storage in automotive and industrial applications. The controller implements the required command set, timing modes, and protocol extensions defined in MMC 4.51, including support for high-speed modes (HS200/HS400 where applicable), boot operations, and enhanced device management features. As a P0 core compliance feature, this ensures the host controller can properly enumerate, configure, and communicate with MMC 4.51-compliant memory devices through the appropriate register configurations in HOSTCONTROL1, CLOCKCONTROL, and TRANSFERMODE registers.

features.name: 3MCR Multi Card Reader
features.description:
## 3MCR Multi Card Reader (F_3MCR)

The 3MCR (Multi Card Reader) is the core SDMMC host controller module that provides a complete interface for communicating with SD, SDIO, and MMC memory cards. It implements the SD Host Controller Standard Specification, featuring a comprehensive register set for command/response handling, data transfer control via PIO or DMA modes, configurable clock generation, and timeout management.

The controller architecture includes dedicated blocks for command control, transmit/receive data paths, a block buffer (FIFO) for data staging, and supports both single and multi-block transfers with programmable block sizes and automatic CRC generation/checking.

features.name: Command Issuing
features.description:
## Command Issuing (F_CMD_ENGINE)

The Command Issuing feature implements the core command control logic that manages the transmission of SD/MMC commands to connected cards through the CMD line interface. This engine handles command serialization, CRC generation, response reception and parsing, and coordinates with the timeout control block to detect command completion or timeout conditions. It interfaces with the COMMAND register (section 57.3.2.7) and ARGUMENT1 register (section 57.3.2.5) to construct and issue commands, storing received responses in the RESPONSEn registers (section 57.3.2.8) while signaling completion status through the interrupt system.

features.name: Auto CMD12
features.description:
## F_AUTO_CMD12: Auto CMD12 Feature

### Purpose
The Auto CMD12 feature enables the SDMMC host controller to automatically issue a CMD12 (STOP_TRANSMISSION) command at the end of a multiple-block data transfer without software intervention. This is a critical command engine optimization that reduces CPU overhead and ensures proper termination of multi-block read/write operations.

### Technical Behavior
When enabled via the Transfer Mode register (TRANSFERMODE), the controller automatically generates and transmits CMD12 after the specified block count has been transferred, properly terminating the multi-block operation. The command control logic (section 57.2.2.7) handles the CMD12 timing and response processing internally, with completion status reported through the normal interrupt status mechanism to indicate whether the auto-issued stop command completed successfully or encountered an error.

features.name: Auto CMD23
features.description:
## F_AUTO_CMD23 (Auto CMD23)

### Purpose
The Auto CMD23 feature enables the SDMMC host controller to automatically issue a CMD23 (SET_BLOCK_COUNT) command prior to executing a multi-block read or write operation, without requiring separate software intervention for each command sequence.

### Behavior
When enabled via the Transfer Mode register (TRANSFERMODE), the controller automatically prepends CMD23 to multi-block data transfer commands (CMD18 for read, CMD25 for write), using the value in the Argument 2 register (SDMASYSADDR) as the block count parameter. This hardware-automated command sequencing reduces software overhead, improves transfer efficiency, and ensures proper block count pre-definition as required by SD/eMMC specifications for reliable multi-block operations. The feature is particularly important for ADMA2 transfers where predefined block counts enable more deterministic DMA behavior and eliminate the need for open-ended transfers terminated by CMD12.

features.name: Data Transfer
features.description:
## F_DATA_TRANSFER: Data Transfer

**Description:**
The Data Transfer feature encompasses the core data movement capabilities of the SDMMC Controller, enabling read and write operations between the host system and SD/MMC cards. This includes support for both PIO (Programmed I/O) and DMA transfer modes, utilizing the block buffer for data staging, and managing single-block and multi-block transfers through the Transmit Control and Receive Control blocks. The feature handles data flow through the DATAPORT register, manages block size/count configuration via BLOCKSIZE and BLOCKCOUNT registers, and coordinates with the TRANSFERMODE register to configure transfer direction, auto-command execution, and DMA enable settings.

features.name: Non-DMA Transfer (PIO)
features.description:
## Non-DMA Transfer (PIO) (F_NON_DMA)

**Purpose:** Non-DMA Transfer (PIO) enables Programmed I/O data transfers where the CPU directly reads from or writes to the SDMMC controller's Data Port register (DATAPORT) to move data between system memory and the SD/MMC card, without using DMA hardware assistance.

**Behavior:** In PIO mode, the host controller generates Buffer Read Ready or Buffer Write Ready interrupts when the internal block buffer requires servicing, and the CPU must respond by performing sequential accesses to the DATAPORT register to transfer data. Section 57.2.2.3 describes the PIO/DMA controller that manages this process, while section 57.2.6 details the FIFO overrun and underrun conditions that can occur if the CPU cannot service the buffer quickly enough during non-DMA transfers.

features.name: SDMA Transfer
features.description:
## F_SDMA: SDMA Transfer

**Purpose:** SDMA (Single-operation DMA) Transfer enables automated data movement between system memory and the SDMMC controller's block buffer without continuous CPU intervention, using a simple linear addressing scheme for single-block or multi-block transfers.

**Behavior:** The SDMA system operates through the SDMASYSADDR register (57.3.2.2), which holds the system memory address for DMA transfers. When a data transfer is initiated with DMA enabled in the Transfer Mode register, the controller automatically reads from or writes to the specified memory address, generating a DMA interrupt at block boundaries to allow the host driver to update the system address for the next data segment. This mechanism, described in the PIO/DMA controller block (57.2.2.3), handles FIFO management and prevents overrun/underrun conditions (57.2.6) by coordinating data flow between the external memory bus and the internal block buffer.

features.name: ADMA1 Transfer
features.description:
## ADMA1 Transfer (F_ADMA1)

Based on the SPC58 H-Line SDMMC Controller specification, ADMA1 (Advanced DMA version 1) Transfer is a DMA mode that provides enhanced data transfer capabilities compared to basic SDMA by supporting descriptor-based scatter-gather operations with a simplified 32-bit descriptor format. ADMA1 allows the host controller to automatically process a linked list of descriptors, enabling transfers to/from non-contiguous memory regions without CPU intervention, though with the limitation of 4KB page-aligned boundaries. This mode is configured through the DMA Select field in the Host Control 1 register (HOSTCONTROL1) and operates in conjunction with the ADMA System Address register to manage descriptor fetching and data movement.

features.name: ADMA2 Transfer
features.description:
Based on the SPC58 H-Line Reference Manual for the SDMMC Controller (3MCR), here is the description for the ADMA2 Transfer feature:

## F_ADMA2: ADMA2 Transfer

**Description:** ADMA2 (Advanced DMA version 2) Transfer provides an enhanced DMA mechanism that uses descriptor tables in system memory to define scatter-gather data transfers, allowing non-contiguous memory buffers to be transferred efficiently without CPU intervention. The DMA mode is selected via the HOSTCONTROL1 register's DMA Select field, and ADMA2 operations utilize the descriptor-based architecture managed through the PIO/DMA controller block to handle complex multi-block data transfers with automatic address management. This P0-priority feature is essential for high-performance data transfer operations, eliminating the FIFO overrun/underrun conditions that can occur in non-DMA modes by providing autonomous data movement between the block buffer and system memory.

features.name: Multiple Block Transfer
features.description:
## Multiple Block Transfer (F_MULTI_BLOCK)

**Purpose:** This feature enables the SDMMC controller to transfer multiple consecutive data blocks in a single operation, significantly improving throughput for large data transfers to/from SD/MMC cards.

**Behavior:** Multiple block transfers are configured through the BLOCKCOUNT register (which specifies the number of blocks to transfer) and the TRANSFERMODE register (which enables multi-block mode and optional block count functionality). The controller automatically manages sequential block addressing and can utilize the Block Gap Control register (BLOCKGAPCONTROL) to pause transfers between blocks if needed, while the hardware handles block counting and transfer completion detection without continuous software intervention.

features.name: Single Block Transfer
features.description:
## Single Block Transfer (F_SINGLE_BLOCK)

Single Block Transfer enables the SDMMC controller to read or write exactly one data block (typically 512 bytes for SD cards) in a single command operation. This mode is configured via the Transfer Mode register (TRANSFERMODE) with the Multi/Single Block Select bit cleared, and the Block Count register (BLOCKCOUNT) set to 1, using commands like CMD17 (READ_SINGLE_BLOCK) or CMD24 (WRITE_BLOCK). This transfer type is fundamental for simple data operations where only one block needs to be accessed, avoiding the overhead of multi-block setup and the requirement for explicit stop commands (CMD12).

features.name: Abort Transaction
features.description:
## Abort Transaction (F_ABORT)

### Purpose
The Abort Transaction feature provides a mechanism to forcibly terminate an ongoing data transfer operation on the SDMMC controller, allowing the host to recover from error conditions, timeouts, or to cancel transfers that are no longer needed.

### Technical Behavior
This feature is typically implemented through the **Software Reset Register (SOFTWARERESET)** which contains bits to reset specific portions of the controller—specifically the command line (RSTCMD) and data line (RSTDAT) reset functions. When a data transfer must be aborted, the host issues an abort command (CMD12 for multi-block transfers) and may need to perform a software reset of the data circuit to clear the data path and restore the controller to a known state. The abort mechanism works in conjunction with the **Block Gap Control Register (BLOCKGAPCONTROL)** which can stop transfers at block boundaries, and the **Present State Register (PRESENTSTATE)** which indicates when command and data lines are available after the abort completes.

features.name: Suspend/Resume
features.description:
## Suspend/Resume (F_SUSPEND_RESUME)

The Suspend/Resume feature enables the host controller to temporarily halt an ongoing multi-block data transfer at a block gap boundary and later resume it, allowing the host to service higher-priority operations or manage bus arbitration in multi-card scenarios. This functionality is controlled through the **Block Gap Control register (BLOCKGAPCONTROL)**, which provides bits to request a stop at the next block gap and to subsequently continue the suspended transfer.

When a suspend is requested, the controller completes the current block transfer, pauses at the gap, and signals the host via interrupt; the host can then issue CMD52 (for SDIO) or CMD12 to formally suspend the card before resuming with the appropriate continue command or register write.

features.name: Interrupt System
features.description:
## Interrupt System (F_INTERRUPT)

The SDMMC Controller implements a comprehensive interrupt system that signals the host processor about various controller events including command completion, data transfer completion, buffer ready states, card insertion/removal, and error conditions. The interrupt architecture uses status registers (Normal Interrupt Status and Error Interrupt Status) combined with corresponding enable registers to allow selective masking of individual interrupt sources. This system enables efficient event-driven operation for both PIO and DMA transfer modes, eliminating the need for continuous polling while providing immediate notification of transfer completion, timeouts, CRC errors, and other critical events requiring software attention.

features.name: Normal Interrupts
features.description:
## Normal Interrupts (F_NORMAL_INT)

Normal Interrupts in the SDMMC Controller represent the standard operational interrupt sources that signal successful completion of expected events during SD/MMC card transactions. These interrupts are managed through the Normal Interrupt Status register (NORMALINTSTATUS) and include events such as command complete, transfer complete, buffer read/write ready, card insertion/removal, and DMA interrupt conditions.

The host software enables specific normal interrupts via the Normal Interrupt Status Enable and Normal Interrupt Signal Enable registers, allowing selective notification of completed operations without polling. When enabled and triggered, these interrupts facilitate efficient programmed I/O and DMA-based data transfers by signaling the CPU only when attention is required for the next phase of a transaction.

features.name: Error Interrupts
features.description:
## Error Interrupts (F_ERROR_INT)

Based on the SDMMC Controller (3MCR) specification for the SPC58 H-Line, Error Interrupts provide notification mechanisms for various fault conditions that can occur during SD/MMC card operations. These interrupts signal error events such as command timeout, command CRC errors, command end bit errors, command index errors, data timeout, data CRC errors, data end bit errors, and FIFO overrun/underrun conditions as described in section 57.2.6.

The Error Interrupt functionality is managed through dedicated interrupt status and enable registers (referenced in section 57.3.2.17-57.3.2.18), allowing software to detect, mask, and respond to specific error conditions during command execution and data transfers. As a P0 priority feature under the parent interrupt system (F_INTERRUPT), these error notifications are critical for implementing robust error handling and recovery mechanisms in the host driver software.

features.name: Wakeup Event
features.description:
## Wakeup Event (F_WAKEUP)

The Wakeup Event feature enables the SDMMC controller to generate interrupt signals that can wake the system from low-power states when specific card-related events occur. This functionality is configured through the Wake Up Control Register (WAKEUPCONTROL), which allows enabling wakeup on card insertion, card removal, or card interrupt conditions.

When enabled, these wakeup events trigger the normal interrupt status mechanism (as a child of F_INTERRUPT) while simultaneously asserting a wakeup signal to the system power management logic, allowing the host to resume operation and service the SD/MMC card without requiring the system to remain in an active power state during idle periods.

features.name: Clock Control
features.description:
## Clock Control (F_CLOCK_CONTROL)

The Clock Control feature manages the SD clock generation and distribution to connected SD/MMC cards through the CLOCKCONTROL register, enabling software to start/stop the clock signal, select clock frequencies via divider settings, and monitor clock stability. This feature interfaces with the internal clock generator block (section 57.2.2.5) to provide programmable clock frequencies within the supported frequency range (section 57.2.5), which is essential for proper card initialization sequences and data transfer operations. As a P0 priority feature, it provides fundamental clock domain control including internal clock enable, SD clock output enable, and clock divider configuration for meeting various SD/MMC timing specifications.

features.name: SDCLK Frequency Select
features.description:
## SDCLK Frequency Select (F_SDCLK_FREQ_SEL)

**Purpose:** This feature controls the frequency divider settings for the SD Card Clock (SDCLK) output signal, allowing software to configure the appropriate clock speed for SD/MMC card communication during initialization and data transfer phases.

**Behavior:** The SDCLK Frequency Select field within the Clock Control Register (CLOCKCONTROL) specifies a divisor value applied to the base clock to generate the SDCLK frequency. During card initialization, a lower frequency (typically 400 kHz or less) must be selected, while higher frequencies (up to the card's maximum supported rate) can be configured after successful initialization. The clock generator block (section 57.2.2.5) uses this programmed divisor to produce the appropriate SDCLK output within the supported frequency range defined in section 57.2.5.

features.name: Power Control
features.description:
## F_POWER_CONTROL (Power Control)

The Power Control feature manages the SD card bus power supply through the **Power Control Register (POWERCONTROL)**, enabling the host controller to turn the SD card power on or off and select the appropriate voltage level for the connected card. This is a fundamental P0 priority feature required for proper card initialization, as the SD/MMC specification mandates specific power sequencing during card detection and enumeration. The controller uses this register to control the external power supply circuitry, supporting voltage switching between different levels (typically 3.3V and 1.8V) as required by the card type and operating mode.

features.name: Speed Mode Support
features.description:
## Speed Mode Support (F_SPEED_MODES)

This feature provides support for multiple SD/MMC bus speed modes, enabling the SDMMC controller to operate at different clock frequencies and data transfer rates as defined by SD/MMC specifications. The controller supports Default Speed (DS), High Speed (HS), and potentially UHS-I speed modes, with the Clock Control register (CLOCKCONTROL) managing clock frequency selection and the Host Control 1 register (HOSTCONTROL1) configuring the high-speed enable bit for mode switching. Speed mode configuration directly impacts the maximum achievable data throughput and must be coordinated with proper voltage signaling levels and card capability negotiation.

features.name: Default Speed (25 MHz)
features.description:
## F_DEFAULT_SPEED: Default Speed (25 MHz)

**Purpose:** This feature implements the baseline SD card operating mode where the SDMMC controller operates the SD bus clock at up to 25 MHz, providing standard data transfer rates as defined by the SD specification for backward compatibility with all SD/MMC cards.

**Behavior:** The Default Speed mode is configured through the Clock Control Register (CLOCKCONTROL) by setting the appropriate SDCLK Frequency Select bits to achieve a 25 MHz clock output. This mode uses single data rate (SDR) signaling on the 4-bit data bus, yielding a maximum theoretical throughput of 12.5 MB/s, and serves as the mandatory fallback mode that all compliant cards must support during initialization and normal operation.

features.name: High Speed (50 MHz)
features.description:
## High Speed (50 MHz) - F_HIGH_SPEED

### Description
The High Speed mode enables the SDMMC Controller to operate at clock frequencies up to 50 MHz, providing enhanced data transfer rates compared to the default speed mode (25 MHz). This mode is configured through the Host Control 1 register (HOSTCONTROL1) by setting the High Speed Enable bit, and requires proper clock divider configuration in the Clock Control register (CLOCKCONTROL) to achieve the target 50 MHz frequency within the controller's supported frequency range.

### Technical Details
When High Speed mode is enabled, the controller doubles the maximum clock frequency from the default 25 MHz to 50 MHz, effectively doubling the theoretical data throughput for SD card communications. The clock generator block must be properly configured to derive the 50 MHz clock from the base clock source while maintaining signal integrity requirements for high-speed SD card interface timing.

features.name: UHS-I SDR12
features.description:
## UHS-I SDR12 (F_UHS_SDR12)

**Feature Description:**

UHS-I SDR12 is the baseline Ultra High Speed mode for SD cards operating at 1.8V signaling, providing Single Data Rate transfers at a maximum clock frequency of 25 MHz with a theoretical throughput of up to 12.5 MB/s. This mode serves as the mandatory fallback UHS-I speed mode that all UHS-I compliant cards and hosts must support, ensuring basic interoperability when higher speed modes cannot be negotiated.

The SDR12 mode is configured through the Host Control 2 register's UHS Mode Select field and requires successful completion of the 1.8V signaling voltage switch sequence before operation, as specified in the SD Physical Layer Specification for UHS-I interface timing requirements.

features.name: UHS-I SDR25
features.description:
## UHS-I SDR25 (F_UHS_SDR25)

**Feature Description:**

UHS-I SDR25 is a Ultra High Speed mode that operates using Single Data Rate signaling at 50 MHz clock frequency, achieving a maximum bus speed of 50 MB/s on a 4-bit data bus. This mode requires 1.8V signaling voltage (enabled through the Host Control 2 register's 1.8V Signaling Enable bit) and represents the baseline UHS-I speed grade that doubles the throughput of legacy High Speed mode while maintaining single-edge data sampling.

The SDR25 mode is configured through the UHS Mode Select field in the Host Control 2 register and requires successful completion of the voltage switching sequence from 3.3V to 1.8V signaling before operation.

features.name: UHS-I SDR50
features.description:
## UHS-I SDR50 (F_UHS_SDR50)

**Feature Description:**

UHS-I SDR50 is a Ultra High Speed mode that operates using Single Data Rate signaling at 100 MHz clock frequency, achieving a maximum data transfer rate of 50 MB/s on the SD bus. This mode requires 1.8V signaling voltage (enabled through the voltage switching sequence) and utilizes the standard 4-bit data bus width with data sampled on the rising edge of the clock only.

SDR50 mode is configured through the Host Control 2 register's UHS Mode Select field and requires the controller to support the 1.8V signaling capability indicated in the Capabilities register. The mode may optionally use tuning to optimize sampling point timing, depending on the controller implementation and signal integrity requirements at the 100 MHz operating frequency.

features.name: UHS-I SDR104
features.description:
## UHS-I SDR104 (F_UHS_SDR104)

**Feature Description:**

UHS-I SDR104 is the highest performance Ultra High Speed mode supported by the SDMMC controller, enabling single data rate transfers at up to 208 MB/s using a 208 MHz clock frequency on the SD interface. This mode requires 1.8V signaling voltage (achieved through the voltage switching procedure) and utilizes the 4-bit data bus width with tuning to compensate for signal timing variations at these high frequencies.

SDR104 mode is configured through the UHS Mode Select field in the Host Control 2 register, and the controller must successfully complete the tuning procedure (using CMD19) to calibrate the sampling point before data transfers can reliably operate at this speed. The Capabilities register indicates whether the host controller supports SDR104 mode, and proper clock divider settings in the Clock Control register are required to achieve the target 208 MHz operation.

features.name: UHS-I DDR50
features.description:
## UHS-I DDR50 (F_UHS_DDR50)

**Description:**
UHS-I DDR50 is an Ultra High Speed mode that enables double data rate (DDR) signaling at 50 MHz clock frequency, achieving an effective data transfer rate of up to 50 MB/s by sampling data on both rising and falling clock edges. This mode operates at 1.8V signaling voltage and requires the host controller to configure the UHS Mode Select field in the Host Control 2 register to enable DDR operation with the appropriate timing parameters. DDR50 provides improved throughput compared to SDR modes while maintaining compatibility with UHS-I SD cards that support this speed class.

features.name: Boot Operation
features.description:
## Boot Operation (F_BOOT_OP)

Based on the SDMMC Controller (3MCR) specification for the SPC58 H-Line, the Boot Operation feature enables the host controller to support MMC boot mode, allowing the system to boot directly from an eMMC/MMC device. This functionality permits the controller to read boot data from the MMC card's boot partition during system initialization, typically using a pre-boot or alternative boot sequence defined by the MMC specification. The feature is essential for embedded systems requiring fast, reliable boot-from-flash capability without requiring a separate boot ROM or external memory interface.

features.name: Alternative Boot Mode
features.description:
## Alternative Boot Mode (F_ALT_BOOT)

**Purpose:** Alternative Boot Mode provides a secondary boot mechanism for eMMC devices that differs from the mandatory boot mode, allowing the host controller to initiate boot operations using a different command sequence where CMD0 with argument 0xFFFFFFFA is used instead of holding CMD low.

**Behavior:** In Alternative Boot Mode, the SDMMC controller initiates the boot sequence by sending a specific boot command rather than using the continuous CMD line assertion method. This mode is configured through the HOSTCONTROL2 register's boot-related fields and the MMCBOOT register, enabling the controller to read boot data from the eMMC device's boot partition using standard command/response protocols while still supporting boot acknowledgment detection and boot data transfer completion signaling.

**Context:** As a child feature of F_BOOT_OP, this provides an alternative approach to eMMC boot operations that may be preferred in certain system configurations or when the mandatory boot mode's CMD line timing requirements cannot be met.

features.name: Software Reset
features.description:
## F_SOFTWARE_RESET (Software Reset)

**Purpose:** The Software Reset feature provides software-controlled reset capability for the SDMMC Controller, allowing the host driver to reset specific functional blocks or the entire controller without requiring a hardware reset.

**Behavior:** This feature is implemented through the Software Reset Register (SOFTWARERESET) as described in section 57.3.2.17, enabling selective reset of controller components such as the command line, data line, or a complete controller reset. When triggered, the reset operation clears pending operations, resets internal state machines, and returns the affected blocks to their initial state, which is essential for error recovery scenarios or reinitializing the controller during runtime without affecting the entire system.

features.name: Timeout Control
features.description:
## Timeout Control (F_TIMEOUT_CONTROL)

The Timeout Control feature manages the data timeout counter in the SDMMC host controller, which monitors the interval between data transfers on the DAT line to detect communication failures with SD/MMC cards. It uses a configurable timeout value (set via the TIMEOUTCONTROL register) that determines the maximum allowable time for data line activity, generating a Data Timeout Error interrupt if the card fails to respond within the specified period. This mechanism is essential for robust error handling, preventing the host controller from waiting indefinitely when cards become unresponsive or are removed during data operations.

features.name: Capabilities Register
features.description:
## Capabilities Register (F_CAPABILITIES)

The Capabilities Register is a read-only control register that reports the hardware capabilities and supported features of the SDMMC host controller, including supported voltage levels, maximum block length, base clock frequency, timeout clock frequency, and DMA support capabilities. This register allows software to query the controller's fixed hardware configuration at runtime to properly initialize and configure the host controller for communication with SD/MMC cards. As a P0 priority control feature, it is essential for system initialization since drivers must read these capabilities before configuring operational parameters like clock speeds, power settings, and transfer modes.

features.name: Preset Value Registers
features.description:
## Preset Value Registers (F_PRESET_VALUES)

The Preset Value Registers provide pre-configured settings for different SD/MMC speed modes, allowing the host controller to automatically apply optimal clock divider, driver strength, and other timing parameters when switching between speed modes (such as Default Speed, High Speed, SDR12, SDR25, SDR50, SDR104, and DDR50). These registers eliminate the need for software to manually calculate and configure timing parameters for each speed mode, enabling faster and more reliable mode transitions.

When the Preset Value Enable bit is set in the Host Control 2 register, the controller automatically loads the appropriate preset values based on the selected UHS mode, streamlining speed mode configuration and ensuring compliance with SD specification timing requirements.

features.name: 1.8V Signaling
features.description:
## 1.8V Signaling (F_VOLTAGE_SWITCH)

This feature enables the SDMMC controller to switch from the default 3.3V signaling voltage to 1.8V signaling, which is mandatory for Ultra High Speed (UHS) modes such as SDR50, SDR104, and DDR50. The voltage switching sequence is controlled through the Power Control register (POWERCONTROL), which manages the SD Bus Voltage Select field and coordinates the signaling voltage transition with the connected SD card. This capability is essential for achieving higher data transfer rates while reducing power consumption, as UHS-I cards require 1.8V signaling to operate in their enhanced speed modes.

features.name: 4-bit Data Bus
features.description:
## 4-bit Data Bus (F_4BIT_MODE)

This feature enables the SDMMC controller to transfer data using a 4-bit wide data bus (DAT[3:0]) instead of the default 1-bit mode, providing up to 4x improvement in data throughput. The data bus width is configured through the **Host Control 1 register (HOSTCONTROL1)** by setting the Data Transfer Width bit, which switches the controller between 1-bit and 4-bit data transfer modes. This capability is essential for achieving higher performance with SD cards that support wider bus widths, as specified in the SD Memory Card specification.

features.name: 8-bit Data Bus (MMC)
features.description:
## 8-bit Data Bus (MMC) (F_8BIT_MODE)

**Purpose:** This feature enables the SDMMC controller to operate with an 8-bit wide data bus when interfacing with MMC (MultiMediaCard) devices, doubling the data transfer bandwidth compared to the standard 4-bit mode.

**Behavior:** The 8-bit data bus mode is configured through the Host Control 1 register (HOSTCONTROL1), specifically using the Extended Data Transfer Width bit. When enabled, the controller utilizes all 8 data lines (DAT[7:0]) for parallel data transfers, which is a capability specific to MMC/eMMC devices as SD cards are limited to 4-bit maximum bus width. This mode is essential for achieving high-speed data throughput in embedded MMC applications, particularly when operating in HS200 or HS400 modes.

features.name: LED Control
features.description:
## LED Control (F_LED_CONTROL)

Based on the SDMMC Controller specification, the LED Control feature provides a mechanism to indicate SD/MMC card activity through an external LED signal. This functionality is typically controlled via a bit in the **Host Control 1 register (HOSTCONTROL1)**, which allows software to enable or disable the LED output that reflects bus activity such as data transfers or command operations.

The LED control signal is part of the bus interface group and serves as a visual indicator for system designers to monitor card access status, commonly used during debugging or to provide user feedback about storage device activity on the SD/MMC bus.
